payload.goal: An operator always knows whether a drive run is alive and how far it has got — in the calling session, on the status bar, and in the sofar apps — without asking an agent or opening another terminal, and one run can never be driven by two drivers at once. Liveness is decided by a machine-local lock the OS releases on exit, never by a heartbeat or a record event; a heartbeat exists only to show presence to remote viewers.

tasks.title: docs/SPEC.md Driver section gains: run liveness (a machine-local exclusion held for the run's life and released by the OS on exit; a fresh start and --resume refuse while it is held), the status bar drive segment, `sofar drive --follow`, and the remote presence contract; acceptance entries. Log a Decision qualifying in-session-drive D2 (no pid in the record, no pid file beside it) BEFORE any code.

Rule on remote presence against the guard-rails before any code: a ping sent only when the repo is linked to sofar cloud, carrying run id, slug, task and state and no user content. Log a Decision on whether it is sync (client side allowed) or telemetry emission (a rail it would have to name), and state that the server half is built in sofar-cloud, not here.

Run lock: the driver holds it from taking the run until run_stopped; a new run and --resume refuse while it is held, naming the live driver's log; a crash or kill -9 releases it, sleep does not. Mechanism within the dependency law (node built-ins; flock would need a dependency and a Decision). Tests: two drivers on one run, kill -9 then resume, leftover artefact after a crash.

`sofar status` (one-shot and --watch) shows a run as running, driver gone (no run_stopped, lock free) or stopped wherever the lock is visible; `sofar drive --stop` against a gone driver says so at once instead of waiting 30s. Tests.

Status bar drive segment: when the session's initiative has a live run, show run state and the task in flight next to done/total; a gone or stopped run shows its reason; within the statusline laws (glyph vocabulary, color law, one line, 10s refreshInterval). rust-core 2.6 statusline parity must include it. Tests.

`sofar drive <slug> --follow`: prints one line per handoff, task status change and run warning; exits on run_stopped AND when the driver's lock is gone, so it can never stay silent over a crashed driver; plain line output usable as a Claude Code Monitor command. Tests.

Protocol block (CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md): after `sofar drive --detach`, the agent watches `sofar drive <slug> --follow` (Monitor where the host has it) and relays needs_user and stop events; hosts without a monitor are told to point the operator at the status bar or `sofar status`. Previous block kept as a shipped version.

Client side, per the 1.2 Decision: a linked repo's driver sends presence at start, on each handoff, on a fixed interval and at stop; nothing when unlinked; never a record event; failures to reach the API never affect the run. Tests with injected fetch.

Server contract handed to sofar-cloud: the TTL after which a driver reads as offline, and what the Mac, iPhone and web apps render for running, offline and stopped. Written here; built in sofar-cloud.

Proof from a live Claude Code session on a throwaway initiative: detach a run; status bar shows it within one refresh; Monitor notifications arrive per handoff; a second --resume while it lives is refused; kill -9 the driver, status shows driver gone, --follow exits, --resume is allowed. Record the numbers.
README + release staged for the user to publish.

payload.text:
RESEARCH (2026-09-17, four parallel agents + local checks) — what beats or changes the first plan.

1. LIVENESS. Keep an OS-released lock; change the mechanism from a listening unix socket to a FILE lock. Sockets fail where --detach is launched from: Claude Code's Linux sandbox seccomp blocks AF_UNIX (anthropics/claude-code#44180), macOS Seatbelt denies bind (#39257; measured EPERM under (deny network*)), kill -9 leaves a stale socket file whose cleanup races (VS Code claimInstance does unlink+retry), and the 104-byte path limit. File lock facts: Node has no lock API (nodejs/node#49256, #54446 closed); macOS O_EXLOCK (0x20)|O_NONBLOCK via fs.openSync works with zero deps — REPRODUCED locally on Node 24.15: busy (EAGAIN) while held and while SIGSTOPped, free after kill -9. Linux has no O_EXLOCK: portable zero-dep option is node:sqlite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE (unflagged since Node 22.13; engines floor is >=18 today) or a flock(1) child. Lock file lives in a per-user machine-local cache dir keyed by run id, never in the repo or an iCloud/Dropbox/SMB path; never unlinked. Rust side must use the SAME primitive (std File::try_lock is flock on Unix, stable since 1.89; if Node uses sqlite, Rust uses rusqlite on the same file). Rejected: pid/hostname-pid files (Bazel #12591, #11020), heartbeat locks (proper-lockfile), pidfd/kqueue exit watching (needs a pid), localhost TCP ports. ADD fencing: run_started is epoch 1, each --resume appends run_adopted {run, epoch:max+1}; a driver seeing a newer adoption in its pre-launch fold or 2s byte scan steps down without run_stopped; stop requests count by log order after the adoption instead of the wall-clock adoptedAt check. One durable fact per takeover, not a heartbeat; covers other machines/users/containers after sync (Kleppmann 2016-02-08; Kafka KIP-98 producer epochs).

2. PROGRESS IN SESSION. Monitor watches are capped at 30 min since Claude Code 2.1.271 (no persistent option; confirmed in this session's Monitor schema) and every notification is a model turn, so --follow under Monitor as the default either goes silent or bills idle turns. Replace with `sofar drive <slug> --await`: one-shot, exits with one line on needs_user, run_stopped or driver gone; the agent runs it with run_in_background (no deadline, zero tokens while waiting). Routine progress goes to zero-cost surfaces: statusline segment (refreshInterval redraws while idle; terminal CLI only — the Claude desktop app ignores statusLine, anthropics/claude-code#41456) and a UserPromptSubmit drive line only when something changed (~50 tokens, next prompt, never wakes). Prototype an asyncRewake PostToolUse hook on Bash(sofar drive *) (wakes an idle session via exit 2) — unverified that multi-hour hook timeouts hold. Codex hooks are stable and on in codex-cli 0.136.0 (verified locally) so Codex can be Tier 2 and SPEC Host tiers is stale. Keep --follow for terminals / opt-in narration. Check in proof: Claude Code stops setsid-detached processes when a background task or session ends. Still rejected: channels (research preview, allowlist), MCP push (2026-07-28 spec replaced resources/subscribe; no host puts updates in model context), posting to the messaging socket (peer-messaging D1).

3. APPS. Nothing replaces local file watch + sofar serve SSE + the doorbell. Mac app: Swift FSEvents on .sofar/initiatives/ (survives git rename) + UniFFI fold (UniFFI 0.32.1: async fns, foreign traits; wrap in AsyncStream); full fold measured 4.3 ms on a 1.09 MB log, so byte-offset folding is optional. GAP: nothing syncs during a run — pushStream is only called by manual `sofar push` (packages/engine/src/cli/cloud.ts:401), so iPhone/web see nothing mid-run; a linked driver must push (debounced) as it appends. Best lock-screen/menu-bar surface: iPhone Live Activity driven by APNs (push-to-start iOS 17.2; shows in the Mac menu bar on macOS 26+; Mac apps cannot create Live Activities; 4 KB payload; ended after 8 h so long runs restart it; a Live Activity cannot fetch, so task titles would transit APNs — needs a content ruling or counts-only). Plus MenuBarExtra in the Mac app and time-sensitive notifications for needs_user/stopped/driver gone. Rejected: LiveStore (total-order rebase clashes with ulid fold), Zero/Electric/PowerSync (Postgres row replication), Convex/InstantDB (hosted DB becomes truth), Automerge/Loro (CRDTs solve a problem the log does not have), WebSocket/WebTransport (no gain over SSE). Borrow from Durable Streams: catch-up then live data on the same SSE, saving a round trip per ring. New Rust crates need a Decision (rust-core D1 allows serde, serde_json, ulid).

4. REMOTE PRESENCE. Keep heartbeat + TTL; connection-based presence loses (driver holds no cloud connection; SSE cannot prove client liveness; half-open sockets hide a sleeping Mac for minutes; VS Code tunnels shows live machines offline). Server: one row per run, state computed at read (last_seen > now - ttl), no sweeper. Driver: ping every 30s ±10% jitter and immediately on start, handoff, wake and stop; 10s AbortSignal timeout; failed pings dropped, never queued; seq/boot nonce. Wake detection: local 5s tick, ping at once when wall clock jumps >2 ticks. TTL 90s (matches doorbell 25s/90s). UX: Running (task · Ns ago) / Not responding ("last seen 14:02 — asleep, offline or crashed", never "offline since") / Stopped (reason) / viewer's own feed stale. Never infer stopped from silence. Privacy: ids only (run, slug, task, state, seq, interval), device name from the existing token, linked repos only with opt-out, one overwritten row, deleted N days after stop, never analytics. Optional product choice: `caffeinate -i -w <pid>` keeps the Mac from idle sleep during a run (not lid close).

payload.chose: 1.1(a): the run lock is an flock-semantics exclusive lock on a file keyed by run id. Rust takes it with std File::try_lock (flock on Unix, LockFileEx on Windows; no new crate under rust-core D1), Swift with flock, Node on macOS with fs.openSync(O_EXLOCK|O_NONBLOCK) (verified 2026-09-17 on Node 24.15 to contend with flock, held through SIGSTOP, released on kill -9). Node on Linux holds it through a flock(1) child tied to the driver until sofar-core binaries ship and take over; where flock(1) is absent the driver keeps today's refusal and says liveness cannot be checked. Windows follows sofar-core. Engines floor stays >=18. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").
payload.over: A listening unix socket (blocked by Claude Code's Linux seccomp and macOS Seatbelt sandboxes, stale socket files after kill -9, 104-byte path limit); node:sqlite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE (needs Node >=22.13 and a rusqlite crate on the Rust side, and SQLite's fcntl locks do not see flock on Linux); pid or hostname-pid files; heartbeat locks (proper-lockfile).
payload.rule: Take the run lock with flock semantics only — never fcntl/lockf, SQLite locks, sockets or pid files — so Node, Rust and Swift contend on the same lock.

payload.because: D2's reasons were that a pid is machine-local in a committed log and a reused pid signals a stranger. An empty file outside the repo carries nothing to commit and nothing to reuse: the kernel releases the lock when the holder dies, so no stale value can ever point at another process.
payload.chose: 1.1(b): QUALIFIES in-session-drive D2 (no pid in the record, no pid file beside it) without overturning it. An empty lock file under the per-user state dir ($XDG_STATE_HOME/sofar or ~/.local/state/sofar), whose liveness answer comes only from whether the OS reports the lock held, is not the pid file D2 forbids. D2's rule stands for pids. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").
payload.over: Reading D2 as forbidding any driver-owned file (leaving no way to tell a live driver from a dead one), or writing a pid into the lock file for diagnostics.
payload.rule: Never write a pid or any content into a run lock file, never place it under the repo, and never unlink it.

payload.because: Telemetry is data about the product's use sent to its maker; this ping is the operator's own run state delivered to the operator's own devices through sync they opted into, the same class as `sofar push`. The conditions make that distinction checkable rather than asserted.
payload.chose: 1.1(c): the driver's presence ping is user-facing sync, not telemetry emission — the CLAUDE.md guard-rail "DO NOT build … telemetry emission" is NAMED here and does not apply to it. payload.because: Ownership is the highest epoch, not the newest id, so the requests a driver must honour are those made after the adoption that put IT in force. Ids are ulids — they carry the time the timestamps did and every reader of the fold compares the same bytes. Changing the element rather than adding an array keeps one list; rust-core mirrors one line.
payload.chose: 2.2 fold shape: RunState gains `adoptions` [{id, ts, epoch}] and `owner` {id, epoch} (run_started's id at epoch 1 until an adoption outranks it), and `stop_requests` now carries event ids instead of envelope timestamps (name unchanged, every other reader used only its length). A stop request is in force when its id sorts after the OWNER's adoption — SPEC's "latest adoption" read as the adoption in force, and SPEC reworded to say so.
payload.over: Cutting at the latest adoption by id (a stale lower-epoch adoption synced in late would silence requests meant for the owner); a parallel `stop_request_ids` array beside the timestamps; keeping the wall-clock adoptedAt compare.
